chunks: And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id informed us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan at-Taymali narrated to us, from al-Abbas ibn Aamir ibn Rabah, from Ibn Bukayr, from al-Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far al-Baqir

saying: 'For the young man (al-Ghulam) there is a disappearance before his rising, and his inheritance is sought after.' I asked: 'Why is that?' He said: 'He fears' and he pointed with his hand to his abdomen. He meant killing.

key_terms.الْمَطْلُوب: The one who is sought after or hunted

ai.seo_question: What is the reason for the Imam's disappearance before his rising according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (as), the term 'al-Ghulam' (the youth) is interpreted by Shia scholars as referring to the Hidden Imam, whose pre-rising occultation involves a protective concealment from assassination, specifically pointing to the threat of being killed by his enemies. This state of hiding ensures that his inheritance (turath) remains a subject of contention and active seeking, highlighting the political and spiritual stakes of his absence. The hadith underscores the divine wisdom behind the Imam's hidden status as a means of preserving his life and authority until the appointed time.
